take_homes: Ask what job the teammate is doing before deciding what to share. Pick context, skill, output or interface against that job, and don't pick whatever our tools happen to support.
A shared agent isn't shared until someone is named to answer for it. The files copy easily, but the owner doesn't.
Talk to one person about how they do the job today before building more, and ask what would have to be true for them to switch.

monday.move: Ask the pricing working group member who reads my pilot-cohort brief how they use it today, and what would make them switch to a shared version. I'll take the person's name from module-7/monday.md.
monday.who: The one person in the pricing working group named in monday.md
monday.when: Monday, a 20-30 minute chat before the working group meets
monday.stop_condition: If they say they never open the brief and use their own spreadsheet, and nothing small would change that, I stop building a shared interface and send them the output only.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files, so everyone keeps their own copy.

misconception.why: I came in thinking better prompts were the skill. This module spent its time on the teammate's job, which of four things to share, and who owns it, and none of that is prompt writing. The prompts were pasted for me, so I haven't properly tested whether prompt quality still matters. I'd say shaken, not changed.

one_line: The middle of it is good if you have a team to hand things to, since it makes you name the person and the owner. The last third mostly repeats the first two.
